messages:
Alex K.: Heads up — GHAS scanner job failing across multiple repos this morning, looks like Trivy step times out while trying to access the cache. full log below

Alex K.: ```
ERROR: trivy: failed to acquire cache lock: context deadline exceeded
2026-03-20T08:01:12Z scanner-runner: exit status 1
```

Dina S.: Ugh, seen this before when the cache backend (redis) had eviction/connection churn. Any recent infra changes? @Matt H.

Matt H.: We rotated the redis creds last night for the ci-cache cluster and switched the client config to use TLS verification. No errors in infra alerts though. Will check runner logs.

sec-ci-bot: GitHub Actions workflow #scan-main@v4 failed for repo: infra/helm-charts — runner: self-hosted-ubuntu-12 — job: trivy-scan — code: 1

Alex K.: Also seeing failures specifically when scanning large node_modules tarball images — maybe lock contention when multiple scans run concurrently on same cache key.

Dina S.: Two things to consider: short-term mitigation = increase lock timeout / fallback to no-cache for affected runs. Long-term = move to object-store-based cache (S3) with advisory locks, or per-repo cache keys.

Rachel P.: Impact-wise, these failures block scheduled nightly dependency scans and delay triage for ~20 open CVEs. Can we get a workaround so triage continues? Could bypass cache for nightly jobs and still upload sbom/artifacts for auditing?

Matt H.: I can patch the GHAS workflow to set TRIVY_CACHE_DISABLED=true for nightly and re-run. That should avoid the lock path. Will also add a retry wrapper (3x, backoff).

Alex K.: Good. Also question: some of the noisy findings are in vendored JS deps that we already suppress in Snyk. Do we have suppression parity between Snyk and Trivy/GHAS? Right now suppressions live in kyverno-style files in infra but Trivy's policy is separate.

Dina S.: We do not have parity. That's been causing duplicate noisy issues. I propose a suppression mapping job: export Snyk suppression IDs -> sync to trivy-ignore and ghsa-allowlist. Small script can run as part of scanner pipeline.

SRE-Oncall: Quick note: when you disable cache, observability for token-level audit gets less granular. Make sure we keep an artifact upload step so audit logs still contain the SBOM and bytes scanned (we need that for compliance).

Matt H.: Will keep artifact upload. For RBAC/KMS side: one failing runner showed KMS decrypt errors while fetching suppression DB from secret store: `kms: decryption failed`. Might be a race during key rotation.

Dina S.: If suppression DB is encrypted with rotated key, fallback to previous key must be allowed for a short window. @Rachel P. do we have rotation policy that enforces immediate rotate without grace?

Rachel P.: Keys rotate every 30 days with a 48-hour overlap window, but looks like the deploy rolled out a new agent without the old key in its KMS binding. I'll coordinate with infra to add the old key binding back for that service account.

Alex K.: Actionable list: (1) Matt: patch GHAS workflows to disable cache + add retries for nightly scans (ETA 2h). (2) Dina: draft small sync job to mirror Snyk suppressions into trivy-ignore (ETA EOD). (3) Rachel: fix KMS binding rollback for the suppression DB service account (ETA 1h). (4) SRE-Oncall: monitor for recurrence and escalate to infra on-call if more than 5 failures in 1h.

Matt H.: I'll open a PR for the workflow change now and ping once deployed.

Dina S.: For prioritization of patches: let's mark the 20 CVEs blocked by scans as "triage-pending" and prioritize any with public exploit or high CVSS to patch window 48h. I'll produce a short CSV export of vuln list once scans complete.

Alex K.: Sounds good. One follow-up question: can suppression sync also tag findings with source (snyk/trivy) so we don't hide something unique to Trivy? We should only suppress matches that map 1:1.

Dina S.: Yes — sync will include source mapping and only apply ignore for fingerprint matches (package + version + cve). No blanket ignore.

Rachel P.: Thanks all. If infra fixes KMS binding quickly we should be back to normal after nightly runs re-run. @sec-ci-bot please enqueue re-run for affected workflows. :raised_hands:

sec-ci-bot: Enqueued re-run for 8 workflows in infra/* and web/* — prioritized: nightly-scans.

SRE-Oncall: I'll add an alert threshold for trivy cache lock errors so we can detect next time before it hits >10 repos.

Alex K.: Appreciate the quick turnaround — keep updates here and I'll start the triage list when results come in. :thumbsup:
